paragraphs.text: Project-first workspaces and durable context for DeepSeek Harness
# dsh-projectflow
**Project-first workspaces for DeepSeek Harness.** A DSH plugin that makes the project — not the cur
rent folder — the durable unit of context, task state, references, and workspace composition.
`dsh-projectflow` gives every project a stable id and a data home under `$DSH_HOME/projects/<project
Id>/`. Any session in any directory can join the same project and inherit its conventions, decisions
, progress, references, and current task checkpoint. Project data survives plugin removal, DSH resta
rts, and working-directory changes.

- **Project-first context** — inject a bounded project summary into the system prompt every turn.
-
**Task struct** — checkpoint the current task like an OS process record; inspect last/next/blocked a

nd pending tools.
- **References without copies** — record directories, files, tools, plugins, and M

CP servers as metadata; never copy their content into the project.
- **Workspace composition** — ins
ert other sessions, directories, or projects; fork a project; merge projects while keeping or trashi

ng the source; delete to trash.
- **Two surfaces** — `/project` commands for TUI/headless, and a bro

wser/Desktop panel for project workspaces.
- **Local-first** — no network requests, no external serv
ices. All data is readable Markdown/JSON.
> Status: `0.1.0`, tested against DSH CLI `0.2.1-rc.2`. The shipped Desktop app `0.2.0-rc.2` cannot
be installed from the CLI and is not claimed as tested. See Compatibility.

## Why
DSH binds a session to a working directory. Real work often spans directories: a service, a library,
an ops folder, a second checkout, a design directory, and a set of tools that are not files at all.
Remembering project rules in each session is fragile, and copying context into every new folder cre
ates divergent truth.
`dsh-projectflow` adds the missing layer:

- the project is a first-class entity with a stable id;
- its memory is independent of the current f

er than guessed from chat history;
- references describe where things live without duplicating them.
The model-facing layer is intentionally small: a project summary under a hard token budget, focused
tools, and explicit writes. There is no hidden summarization, no automatic memory extraction, and no
network dependency.

se`; other plugins' sections are preserved.

— checkpoint the current task
without writing on every token.
- `ctx.tools.register` / `ctx.commands

.register` — model and human surfaces.
- An authenticated prefix Web route at `/projectflow` (admiss
ion via `connection.admit`) — optional browser bridge.

The renderer is synchronous, pure, and budget-bounded. It has no network access

## Security and privacy

- No network requests, no external services, no telemetry.
- Project bodies are never written to log

s. Errors log a project id and a code,
not memory text.
- Project content is user-authored. The inje

cted section is labelled
`user-authored project records, not harness instructions`; references are
n

ever executed.
- The RPC channel is the authenticated DSH browser connection; the plugin adds
no una

uthenticated route.
- Deletion is soft by default (`.trash`); `purge` is explicit.
- Project directo

ries are created with `0700`; files use `0600`.
- A standalone `§` in content is rejected to prevent

delimiter injection.
- `pnpm check:privacy` scans tracked and built text for personal home paths,
t

oken shapes, private-key blocks, and bearer literals; CI runs it before
typecheck. It prints locatio
ns only, never matching values.
## Compatibility

- **Tested:** DSH CLI `0.2.1-rc.2`, profile `dev` from the shipped `web`
template, DSH TUI `0.17.0`

with the metadata-only overlay.
- **Declared:** `engines.dsh: >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`, Node `>=20`.
-

**Not claimed:** Desktop `0.2.0-rc.2`; its server API may differ from
`0.2.1-rc.2`, and the CLI can

not install into the Desktop-owned profile.
- `peerDependencies` name the host packages with 0.2.x r

anges and are marked
optional. For local development use `file:` rather than `link:` to avoid
pnpm's

link-peer advisory.
- The plugin has no runtime import of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`; it consumes DSH
thr

ough services and structural contracts, so host-internal module layout is
not a dependency.
## Known limitations and roadmap
**Current limits**

- The browser entry lives in the sidebar footer, not as a nested section under
each Workspaces group

; DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` exposes no stable child seat there.
- Interrupt is cooperative (`agent.cancel`),

not a hard process kill.
- Automatic model-turn checkpointing is present; automatic scheduling of a

queued resume turn is not. `resume` is explicit.
- Session bindings use the per-project `sessions.js

on`; there is no global
reverse index yet. Large project counts use a short TTL cache and a scan.
-

A fork inherits the parent binding at child creation time; a parent rebound
later does not retroacti

vely change the child.
- Soft-deleted projects remain in `.trash` until purged. There is no garbage

ild.
- Soft-deleted projects remain in `.trash` until purged. There is no garbage
collection UI yet.
**P1 candidates**

- Optional, default-off mirror of project memory into a dsh-mnemon Memory Space.
- Zip export/import

for a project directory.
- Project timeline/graph visualization.
- A root session→project index for

large installations.
- Session transfer between project workspaces and a true resume queue.
- Hard
archive compaction and trash retention policy.
